- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct, leading to overprediction in subsequent days.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values, particularly when recent history shows downward momentum.
- Mean reversion is underappreciated — model fails to adjust downward when true values show clear downward drift.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows increasing lag: model reacts to recent history but misses medium-term trend reversals.
- Model overfits to recent highs, ignoring longer-term volatility patterns or policy-driven corrections.
- When true values dip sharply (e.g., 70s from 75s), model often fails to recognize the magnitude and delays correction.
- Model underestimates volatility in low-price regimes — tends to smooth out sharp drops, leading to underprediction of true lows.
